summary: Service-account bridge for Data Fabric readonly access across AWS and GCP
description:
Issue summary:
We need a maintainable, least-privilege pattern to let the Data Fabric analytics service access read-only datasets across both AWS and GCP projects. Current ad-hoc approach creates per-team, long-lived cross-account roles and manual key distribution which is hard to audit and prone to privilege creep.

Impact:
- Data Fabric queries require elevated access in multiple cloud accounts; several ad-hoc roles exist with broader than necessary permissions.
- Audit and access reviews flagged unclear ownership and no centralized short-lived credential flow.
- Risk of accidental data exfiltration and difficulty rotating service credentials.

Environment:
- Production Data Fabric cluster (prod - us-east) with downstream read-only jobs hitting AWS accounts (redwood-data-prod) and GCP projects (data-prod-eu).

Requested outcome:
- Design and implement a scoped "service-account bridge" pattern (broker/proxy) that allows a single Data Fabric service identity to assume short-lived credentials in AWS and impersonate a service account in GCP with strictly read-only permissions to required datasets.
- Avoid per-team role explosion; provide mapping configuration per dataset owner in a centralized repo/service.
- Provide audit logs and rotation policy, and document runbook for emergency revocation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a Data Fabric read job for dataset 'analytics.events' that lives in AWS account redwood-data-prod
2) Observe that job uses a long-lived IAM role ARN stored in Secrets Manager
3) Check CloudTrail and see role used regularly without short-lived assumption events
4) Attempt to rotate the role credentials -> job fails, indicating coupling between secret and role mapping
logs: 2026-03-08T14:12:02Z - DataFabricWorker - ERROR - Failed to access s3://redwood-prod-analytics/events - AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/legacy-data-fabric-role/session is not authorized to perform: s3:GetObject
2026-03-09T09:03:50Z - GCP - iam.serviceAccounts - WARNING - Service account impersonation used by redwood-data-fabric@data-prod-eu.iam.gserviceaccount.com with broad scope: roles/storage.admin
investigation_notes: Initial audit found 7 unique long-lived role ARNs in Secrets Manager and 3 GCP service accounts used by Data Fabric jobs.
Owner mapping is stored as free-form YAML in internal repo infra-access which makes automated rotation risky.
Hypothesis: A lightweight broker that issues STS AssumeRole and GCP short-lived impersonation tokens would reduce privilege window and centralize logging.
SRE observation: attempts to rotate one AWS role caused a batch of Data Fabric jobs to fail due to hardcoded role ARN in legacy launchers.
Security noted: at least one GCP SA has roles/storage.admin; needs to be reduced to roles/storage.objectViewer for readonly flows.
comments: Marisol Ortega (reporter) [2026-03-10]: Filing this because Data Platform flagged multiple long-lived credentials during readiness review.

Devon Patel (assignee) [2026-03-11]: Assigned. Next steps: inventory all secrets referencing cross-account roles and draft broker API contract. Booking kickoff with Data Platform and Security on 2026-03-12.

Aisha Khan (Security) [2026-03-11]: Prefer GCP impersonation with domain-restricted principals and short TTL. AWS roles should require external-id enforcement and deny policies to limit write actions.
Ethan Chen (Data Platform) [2026-03-12]: Data Fabric can be updated to call a token broker prior to every job; will prototype patch to use STS and gcloud impersonation with TTL=15m.
proposed_solution: Phase 1 (design): Define broker API and mapping schema. Minimum features: request short-lived AWS creds via AssumeRole (STS), request GCP impersonation token, per-dataset mapping, audit event emission.
Phase 2 (pilot): Implement broker as an internal service behind mTLS, integrate with HashiCorp Vault for credential issuance and rotate legacy secrets to broker-backed tokens.
Phase 3 (rollout): Gradually update Data Fabric job runners to obtain credentials from broker, deprecate legacy role ARNs, and enforce policy via OPA gate on infra deploys.
Fallback/rollback: Keep legacy secrets with a feature flag; if broker returns error, fall back to legacy but emit high-severity alerts for manual intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Broker service deployed to staging and prod with monitoring and audit logs
All Data Fabric read jobs use broker-issued short-lived credentials (TTL <= 30m) in prod - us-east within rollout window
No job requires roles with write permissions; GCP SAs reduced to objectViewer where applicable
Runbook documented in Confluence and an emergency revoke path exists
next_steps: 1) Kickoff design meeting with Security, Data Platform, and SRE (scheduled 2026-03-12)
2) SRE to run inventory script against Secrets Manager and GCP IAM to enumerate existing bindings (assigned: Devon)
3) Draft broker API contract and mapping schema (owner: Data Platform)
4) Create a short-lived pilot for one non-critical dataset and test rotation flow
resolution: Pending: design and pilot planned. No production changes made as of 2026-03-12.
